name: The Chalice
descent_text: No descent has been described for The Chalice itself. It shares its summit and the mid-face crossing ledge with Playing Not Spraying, whose first-ascent party rappelled the southeast side of the peak on a single 70 m rope from natural anchors (trees and horns); plan on the same, and carry extra webbing to build anchors.
approach: The Silver Horn is a sub-summit on the east ridge of Silver Star Mountain, east of the main summit, and both of its routes are on the clean white granite of its south face. That face is not reached from the Wine Spires pullout or Burgundy Col, which serve the other side of the crest. Instead, walk the Cedar Creek Trail from its trailhead at the end of FR 5310-200, off SR-20 about half a mile east of the Klipchuck Campground turnoff. After roughly five miles, turn off to the right below the old burn and follow a rough path up the right-hand side of the creek that drains the south side of the Silver Horn. Meadows at about 6,200 ft give good camping below the face.
overview: An 8-pitch route up the right side of Silver Horn's true South Face, climbing flakes/corners/splitters to a broad mid-height ledge, then the upper face beside a prominent central arete before finishing over blocky ground to the summit.
beta: Begins on the right side of the South Face and follows flakes, corners, and splitters up to a broad ledge roughly halfway up the face. From the ledge, walk leftward to start the upper half of the climb; the first pitch above the ledge heads up to the left side of the most prominent arete/pillar in the middle of the upper face. After two more pitches, the route trends rightward and reaches the summit via blocky ground just right of a prominent chimney.
